title: APPR � Eligible � 1 Adult Pax � Delay Code 61 (Flight Plan) � Booker Basic Member � Accommodation Exceeds $500 Hotel Cap -> Pending Agent Review (Manual)
goal: Verify APPR SOC eligibility, hotel cap evaluation, OCR extraction, and manual review escalation for a single adult passenger with Basic Aeroplan membership experiencing a 7-hour controllable flight plan delay (Code 61), where a submitted hotel receipt of $580.00 CAD exceeds the $500.00 CAD policy hotel cap, triggering routing to the Manual Handling Queue for agent review before any Interac payout issuance.

checkpoints.step: Given the user opens the agentic chatbot
Then the chatbot displays greeting (GLOB-01):
checkpoints.expected: Hello! I will be your virtual assistant today. I can assist you in English or French. Which language would you prefer to use today?

checkpoints.step: When the user selects English
Then an alert information is displayed:
checkpoints.expected: Please note that by using this service, you will interact with an automated chatbot which uses AI to answer your questions and requests. Your personal information will be used to identify and authenticate you, to answer your request, and for other purposes detailed in the Privacy Notice.

checkpoints.step: Then the chatbot asks: "How can I help you today?"
checkpoints.expected: How can I help you today?

checkpoints.step: And the user says: "My flight from Toronto to Vancouver was delayed by 7 hours due to flight plan issues. I had to stay overnight at a hotel and paid out of pocket. Can I get reimbursed?"
checkpoints.expected: My flight from Toronto to Vancouver was delayed by 7 hours due to flight plan issues. I had to stay overnight at a hotel and paid out of pocket. Can I get reimbursed?

checkpoints.step: When the chatbot identifies Standards of Care (SoC) intent
Then the chatbot checks: Is this a third-party submission? -> NO
Then the chatbot displays the case opening legal disclaimer (GenUC-24):
checkpoints.expected: Please note that the assessment and decision regarding your request will be made through an automated decision-making process. To file your claim, you'll need your booking reference, the name associated to the booking and any receipts you'd like to be reimbursed for. If your claim is eligible, you may also need to provide your address, contact information and where you'd like the funds deposited. Would you like to get started?

checkpoints.step: Then the chatbot responds:
checkpoints.expected: I can definitely help you with that. To start I'll just need to know some information to be able to process your request and identify you.

checkpoints.step: And the chatbot responds:
checkpoints.expected: Please provide your full name exactly as it appears on your ticket, including any middle names if applicable.

checkpoints.step: And the user provides "[First Name] [Last Name]"
checkpoints.expected: [First Name] [Last Name]

checkpoints.step: Then the chatbot responds:
checkpoints.expected: Thanks, [First Name]! And, what is your booking reference number?

checkpoints.step: And the user provides "PNR: [PNR Code]"
checkpoints.expected: PNR: [PNR Code]

checkpoints.step: Then the chatbot searches Trip Tracer for PNR: [PNR Code]
And Trip Tracer returns: PNR FOUND (1 Passenger on booking)
Then the chatbot responds:
checkpoints.expected: To keep your account secure and assist you further, I'll need to verify your identity. I'll do this by sending a one-time verification code to either your email or phone number on file. Where would you like to receive it?

checkpoints.step: And the chatbot displays options:
checkpoints.expected: * Email: t***@gmail.com * Phone: +1***789

checkpoints.step: When the user selects "Email: t***@gmail.com"
checkpoints.expected: Email: t***@gmail.com

checkpoints.step: Then the chatbot responds:
checkpoints.expected: I've sent a verification code to your email, please enter it within 15 minutes of receiving it.

checkpoints.step: And the user provides the OTP code "546879"
Then the chatbot validates the OTP code -> CORRECT (attempt 1 of 5)
Then the chatbot responds:
checkpoints.expected: Your verification was successful. Let's proceed to the next step.

checkpoints.step: Then the chatbot checks if this PNR is a group booking -> No
Then the chatbot checks if there are multiple PAX on PNR? -> No (1 PAX)
Then the chatbot retrieves booking details and displays:
checkpoints.expected: I found the following journey: * Flight: AC 301 * Route: Toronto (YYZ) -> Vancouver (YVR) * Date: June 15, 2026 * Departure Delay: 7 hours (420 minutes) * Passengers: 1 Adult Is this the journey you'd like to check?

checkpoints.step: And the user confirms "Yes"
checkpoints.expected: Yes

checkpoints.step: Then the chatbot checks if there is more than 1 segment -> No
Then the chatbot sends request to Case Services for duplicate check (GenUC-10)
And Case Services returns: NO existing case found for this passenger + journey combination
Then the chatbot checks 72-hour window passed -> YES
Then the chatbot verifies Filing deadline limitation:
checkpoints.expected: * Origin: YYZ (Ontario) -> Limitation = 730 days * Destination: YVR (British Columbia) -> Limitation = 1,095 days * Elapsed: Within limitation period -> PROCEED

checkpoints.step: Then the chatbot checks if triage data is available -> YES
Then DDS evaluates backend rules:
checkpoints.expected: * Delay Code: 61 (Flight Operations / Flight Plan Preparation) -> Controllable * Passenger Type: 1 Regular Adult -> Standard handling * Booker Status: Aeroplan Basic Member * Delay Band: DELAY_6_HOURS_OR_MORE (Overnight eligible) * Operating Airline: Air Canada (AC)

checkpoints.step: And DDS assigns Response Code: SoC-APPR-EL-08
Then the system sends case data to CyberSource for fraud screening
And CyberSource returns: GREEN (no fraud indicators detected)
Then the chatbot displays:
checkpoints.expected: Great news! Based on the details of your flight, you are eligible for expense reimbursement. Your flight AC 301 from Toronto to Vancouver was delayed by approximately 7 hours due to flight planning operations. Under the applicable regulations (APPR), you may be reimbursed for reasonable expenses incurred during this disruption.

checkpoints.step: And the chatbot displays the entitlements for 1 passenger:
checkpoints.expected: Based on the length of your disruption (7 hours), you may be eligible for reimbursement in the following categories: * Hotel accommodation: Rate of the day (up to 3 nights, $500.00 maximum per room) * Meals: up to $30.00 CAD * Ground transportation: up to $200.00 CAD * Essential items: up to $30.00 CAD * Communication: up to $30.00 CAD * Parking: up to $50.00 CAD (1 day maximum) Please note that all expenses must have been incurred during the disruption period and supported by valid receipts.

checkpoints.step: Then the chatbot responds:
checkpoints.expected: To process your claim, I'll need you to upload your receipts. Please upload photos or scans of your receipts for any expenses you incurred during the disruption.

checkpoints.step: When the user uploads the hotel receipt ($580.00 CAD):
checkpoints.expected: * Receipt 1: Hotel receipt � $580.00 CAD (1 night accommodation, exceeds $500 cap)

checkpoints.step: Then OCR engine extracts and validates line items:
checkpoints.expected: * Receipt 1 � Hotel Accommodation: - Line item: Hotel stay, 1 night � $580.00 CAD - Date: June 15, 2026 | Category: Hotel | Within disruption window: YES - Cap check: $580.00 > $500.00 max cap -> Exceeds $500.00 hotel cap limit - OCR Result: REVIEW NEEDED (Exceeds $500.00 hotel cap)

checkpoints.step: Then the system evaluates hotel claim value:
checkpoints.expected: * Total Claimed Hotel Amount: $580.00 CAD * Policy Maximum Hotel Cap: $500.00 CAD * System Rule Check: Submitted hotel amount ($580.00 CAD) EXCEEDS the $500.00 CAD auto-approval hotel cap * Outcome: Case flagged for Manual Review (exceeds $500 hotel cap)

checkpoints.step: Then the system creates a case in Case Services:
checkpoints.expected: * DDS response code: SoC-APPR-EL-08 * Eligibility: ELIGIBLE (Pending Review) * Status: Pending Agent Review * Queue: Manual Handling Queue * Reason: Hotel expense exceeds $500.00 cap limit * Receipt images attached: 1 * Fraud screening result: GREEN

checkpoints.step: And the case reference number is provided to the passenger
Then the chatbot responds:
checkpoints.expected: Your claim has been received and submitted for agent review. Here's a summary: * Case Reference: [Case Number] * Total submitted claim amount: $580.00 CAD * Categories: Hotel ($580.00) * Claimed for: 1 Passenger Because your hotel accommodation claim exceeds our automated cap of $500.00 CAD, a customer service agent will review your receipt manually within 30 days.

checkpoints.step: Then the system triggers notification via Adobe
And a manual review confirmation email is sent to the passenger at t***@gmail.com
Then the chatbot prompts to collect payment information in advance:
checkpoints.expected: "To ensure prompt payment once your claim is reviewed and approved, please confirm your payment details."

checkpoints.step: And the chatbot collects:
checkpoints.expected: Country of residence: Canada Payment method: Interac Email address for Interac transfer: [t***@gmail.com]

checkpoints.step: Then the chatbot responds:
checkpoints.expected: Thank you. Your payment details have been saved. If approved by our review team, funds will be sent via Interac e-Transfer to your email.

checkpoints.step: Then the chatbot offers: "Is there anything else I can help you with?"
checkpoints.expected: Is there anything else I can help you with?

checkpoints.step: When the user selects "No"
checkpoints.expected: No

checkpoints.step: Then the chatbot responds "Thank you for choosing Air Canada."
checkpoints.expected: Thank you for choosing Air Canada.
